Name: Tammi F.
Review: We were staying in Amsterdam and wanted to try actual Dutch food. We ended up coming back here afterward because we wanted to try other things on the menu! Fantastic experience, lovely waitstaff and we were very happy with the food. Definitely the best place in the area.

Name: Serene E.
Review: This is definitely a Dutch experience!  Four of us came on a chilly night out and got an adorable table inside the warm and inviting restaurant. They served us wine while we waited for our table. We ordered two of the Dutch meals for two, which is a little bit of everything Dutch. I mean you leave in a food coma, but it's so worth it. The waiters are so friendly and you feel like you are in your mother's home kitchen.  The place is covered in photos of moms!

Name: Jacques I.
Review: Ya gotta have Indonesian food in Amsterdam! My friends and I came here for dinner, as we read that Sampurna was one of the best spots for Indonesian food.  Plus, while we were at the flower market, we saw that it was just right across from it, so already knew where to find it!I am unfamiliar with Indonesian food, but after having had it at Sampurna, I want to learn and EAT more!  We came here without a reservation and fortunately, was able to get seated for the three of us on a weeknight.  The space isn't large, as the dining room is split into two rooms and is on the more narrow side.  The menus are in both Dutch and English and there's a full bar here.Not knowing anything about Indonesian food, I asked the server what she recommended for someone's first time having it.  She recommended the Sate Solo Menu if we all wanted to get something different and not share.  The sate solo menu is a great option for someone who wants to try multiple items, but doesn't have anyone to share it with.  One of my friends is vegan, so couldn't share any of the meat items and my other friend wanted a different kind of entree.  Therefore, the sate solo menu was for me.  Before we ordered our main entree, we were provided complimentary chips.The sate solo menu came with Indonesian fried rice, two chicken skewers, two beef skewers, two goat skewers, spicy chicken in a coconut sauce, steamed veggies in a peanut sauce, mango salad, boiled egg in a spicy sauce, beans with bamboo shoots, cucumber salad and coconut with peanuts.  Doesn't that sounds amazzzzzing?  Well, it was!  It's spendy at nearly 30 bucks, but I think it's worth trying if you want to have a little bit of everything.  Gosh, what did I love the most?  Everything was so tasty and went together very well, with a little bit of sweet, a little bit of sour, a little bit of spice and a little bit of creamy.  It's truly the best of all worlds.  Of the skewers I liked the goat one the best, as the meat was very tender and flavorful with however it was seasoned.  But all of the skewers had a slight grill taste, which added a nice lightness to all the other plates with sauces.  The spicy chicken in a coconut sauce was incredible, as the coconut flavor really came out with spice, which is just how I like curries.  The steamed veggies in a peanut sauce were crispy and light, and would've even liked them without the peanut sauce.  Though, the peanut sauce adds a nice flavor, especially when eaten with a skewer and the fried rice.  Mango salad was refreshing, with a nice, chill to it and added sweetness to the palate.  Again, all the different taste buds really came through with the solo sate menu.  I left full and happy. Indonesian food, I need to eat you again!  We all loved our food and Sampurna was definitely one of the best meals I had while in Amsterdam.  I loved the various flavors, complementing one another in my meal.  I highly recommend the sate solo menu if you don't do family style here.

Name: Maria F.
Review: They certainly don't skimp on the meals; I couldn't finish the massive burger I was served. Food was really good. The place was crowded, but we lucked out on our timing: we didn't have a reservation but there was one free table. Would come back again. I wouldn't call this a "family friendly" place: it was mostly a younger, singles crowd, dark interior, louder background music. But older kids (10 and up) would be fine.

Name: Samuel A.
Review: This place was recommend by the hotel concierge and it did not disappoint.  The staff was polite, professional, and patient.  The I travel with was really happy with our meals. I had the Seafood Risotto and spinach.  The Risotto was cooked to perfection and the shrimps, clams, and scallop were delicious.  I highly recommend you try this Dutch restaurant out if you are in Amsterdam

Name: Athena C.
Review: See why the hype is all about, this is a down to earth authentic feel to the restaurant. Food tasted straight from Mama's kitchen.

Name: Amber R.
Review: Great place to get a traditional Dutch meal! Love the vibe and staff there. If it's your first time having Dutch food, it might be a good idea to get the family-style dinner because it includes a small portion of everything. Make sure you order the beers there too!

Name: Luke S.
Review: Excellent breakfast food place! Went three times while visiting Amsterdam and everything was superb. Loved their pancakes, sandwiches, and deserts. Large portions and every tastes great. The service is a little slow as they are crazy busy all the time. Highly recommended!

Name: Brian R.
Review: This is a hugely popular place that has a bit of a wait but was totally worth it! The food is delicious and plated perfectly. I didn't have the pancakes but they looked spectacular. My stack of House hash browns and poached eggs with salmon was tasty and creative! Look at the way my son's sandwich showed up (see photo). Old school paper/string wrap. Very cool. They had a nice DIY mimosa too. Fresh OJ all the way and your own mini-split of bubbly!The staff was great. If you're looking for breakfast, brunch, or lunch you can't go wrong.

Name: Tim X.
Review: It was around the corner from our AirBnB on Ten Katenstraat, and there's plenty of choices. We tried the Vietnamese place (Viet View), supposedly "Street Food" but it wasn't quite what we expected - the bowls were a little too salted with soy and there was no soup. The Banh Mi was decent and filling, good choice.The standout was Jabugo, where they had Jamon Iberico de Bellotta and some really good manchego, both of excellent quality, albeit quite pricey.A great place to eat if you are around the area.

Name: Emma W.
Review: Great food and amazing service.I'm not a good writer and don't know how to write hundreds of words in admiration of a place but I must say that it was better than expectations. I ordered a Tomato soup and Goat cheese croquettes for a warm starter and for the main course I had a steak. The quantity was good but I guess they can work a bit more on the quality of the ingredients. Also, the staff was very friendly and professional.

Name: Mike H.
Review: The food was just okay. Besides the spareribs (the only dish we liked), the other dishes were disappointing. The spinach mash potato in our hutspot was really dry to the point that I could hardly eat it without pouring and mixing with all of the gravy. The meat that came with it was definitely over salted. The Moeder's veggie tasted like Thai curry with a strong flavor from lemongrass. Even for rustic dining, food overall tasted one dimensional and lacked refinement. We also did not expect the place to be completely filled with tourists and seating arrangements to be so cramped that you constantly have move over for other guests to get by. It's not hard to tell that its popularity has overgrown its dining capacity over the years. Having said that, I wouldn't recommend going out of the way just to come here.

Name: Jim A.
Review: They are not kidding about having the best ribs. This place has been doing it for 40 years and they have it down perfect. We had the combo plain and smoked rib platter. Nothing left but cleaned bones.Washed it down with a wheat and a trippel

Name: Stephen Y.
Review: Breakfast was good, enjoyed the pancakes and service. Pancakes were light and fluffy with a pleasant surprise of blueberries in the middle. Ordered five stacks, and shared with my daughter. Neither of us finished the pancakes because we were full.

Name: Stella T.
Review: We walked in on a whim, no reservations. The place was jam packed! The friendly hostess was very accommodating in getting us seated fairly quickly. We ordered drinks which came out quick & really spot on perfectly made. The menu is in correlation with the namesake, lots of meat offerings. I ordered the classic burger & the bf ordered ribs. My burger was a tad salty but really good but his ribs! Oooooh man! Those were some serious finger licking ribs! We really enjoyed ourselves here & I highly recommend checking this place out. It's only fair that I pass on the baton since I found this gem through yelp.

Name: Stella T.
Review: We walked in on a whim, no reservations. The place was jam packed! The friendly hostess was very accommodating in getting us seated fairly quickly. We ordered drinks which came out quick & really spot on perfectly made. The menu is in correlation with the namesake, lots of meat offerings. I ordered the classic burger & the bf ordered ribs. My burger was a tad salty but really good but his ribs! Oooooh man! Those were some serious finger licking ribs! We really enjoyed ourselves here & I highly recommend checking this place out. It's only fair that I pass on the baton since I found this gem through yelp.

Name: Earl H.
Review: Amsterdam isn't exactly a culinary wonderland but it has some local flavors you shouldn't miss. The Pantry serves up typical Dutch cuisine with some of the friendliest service you'll find in Amsterdam.   I went for the zuurkoolstamppot which is Sauerkraut mixed into mashed potatoes with a sausage. Nothing exciting to look at but it was actually pretty delicious. If you're in Amsterdam I'd highly recommend making reservations and give the pantry a shot.

Name: Shannen C.
Review: Foodhallen was a cool place to grab food and drinks. The place was pretty busy on Wednesday night. Here are some pros and cons of Foodhallen:ProLots of different types of food to choose from.All the foods we tried were tasty and look and tasted fresh. Gin and Tonic bar was amazing, really refreshing and tasty gin and tonic drinks, unlike any Gin and Tonic I had in the States. Awesome vibe! ConHad a hard time finding an open seat after we get our food.A lot of food vendors only take card, no cash option. I guess this is pretty common.Felt like the prices were higher.Overall, fun food and drink experience in Amsterdam and recommend everyone!

Name: Lauren F.
Review: I came in for breakfast on a Friday morning and was seated after a very minimal wait. Even though it was probably not the thing to get, I ordered the Huevos Rancheros because it sounded the most appetizing at the moment. I was not disappointed. It was a simple combination of eggs, beans, avocado, tortilla and salsa, but I was satisfied. Paired with a matcha latte (for the wake up) and a salted caramel white Russian (for fun...it was Friday after all), I was quite happy with my breakfast at Bakers & Roasters.The design scheme was clean, breakfast place and it was busy but I felt like I got everything in time. Service was efficiently friendly and I paid with a chip card. I would come back to try the other coffee options. They appear to be coffee experts, so I'd check that out.

Name: Michael N.
Review: Excellent evening at Van Speyk. It was recommended by our hotel concierge as we wanted something with good Dutch cuisine. Had the beef stew which was perfect for a cold Amsterdam night. Very friendly and attentive service.

Name: John T.
Review: Man o man - goooood ribs !I'm a certified BBQ judge in the US & I'm here to tell you the ribs are incredible! The slaw was fantastic as well. (I'm not really a big slaw eater, but it was SO Good, I ate it all). While waiting you must visit their pub across the street as well - great drinks- Highly recommend...

Name: Jane K.
Review: Great food and incredible service! Checked it out because it was close to the Renaissance Hotel and was probably my favorite meal of my trip in Amsterdam.Even the appetizer bread and butter tasted better than normal. For seafood, try the oysters (bigger and super juicy) or the Dutch sole.For dessert, cheesecake is a must! They forgot to give my dad his coffee, but instead of just removing it from the check, they also served him one on the house.

Name: Daniel F.
Review: Pretty good burger and meat for Europe in an American style joint. The fries are good. Overall a solid experience. It wasn't the best but bang for buck it's pretty good.

Name: Brian R.
Review: This is a hugely popular place that has a bit of a wait but was totally worth it! The food is delicious and plated perfectly. I didn't have the pancakes but they looked spectacular. My stack of House hash browns and poached eggs with salmon was tasty and creative! Look at the way my son's sandwich showed up (see photo). Old school paper/string wrap. Very cool. They had a nice DIY mimosa too. Fresh OJ all the way and your own mini-split of bubbly!The staff was great. If you're looking for breakfast, brunch, or lunch you can't go wrong.

Name: David N.
Review: With a significant Indonesian population in Amsterdam, we made it a point to partake while we were visiting. We tried making a reservation online for a Monday evening, but nothing was available, so we decided to chance it and walk-in anyway. We arrived to a busy, but not quite full, restaurant and were seated right away. Our first impressions were of awe and appreciation: the interior was slick yet classy, simple but tasteful. We were also delighted that most of the staff was lgbt =)We love spicy, so at the recommendation of our server, we ordered the Kuning Rice Table. Why not try a little of everything? The next hour was an explosion of flavor that would leave us reminiscing for days. From the shrimp soup appetizer to the amazing array of skewers to the spiced coconut to the classic rendang...everything was wonderfully seasoned, cooked, and presented. At about 30 euros/person, it wasn't a cheap meal, but it was definitely worth it as a delicious treat.We ended up cleaning our plates and left fully stuffed and satisfied. The entire waitstaff was friendly, helpful, and wore shining smiles. We definitely recommend this fantastic restaurant, and we look forward to returning in the near future!

Name: Natalie P.
Review: Amazing food and service was great. Would definitely come back again. The asparagus appetizer is a must try.

Name: Marian M.
Review: It was really late at night, we just arrived to Amsterdam from Bergen. There were not many options but as foodies, dinner its a big deal for us. Cannibale Royale is a trendy-rock bar with very tasty bitterbals, burgers and great beer.Era muy tarde a la noche, recién llegabamos de Brujas a Amsterdam. No había muchas opciones pero como foodies, la cena es un tema para nosotros. Cannibale Royale es un bar trendy-rockero con muy sabrosas "bitterbals", hamburguesas y gran selección de cervezas.

Name: Tim J.
Review: Molders is Dutch for Mothers. People were encouraged over the years to bring in pictures of the years of their moms. You see all over pics of peoples moms. Pictures give it that home-like feel. The food here was awesome. I recommend trying everything. And leave room for dessert. You won't be disappointed.

Name: Annette C.
Review: Super cool place with lots of restaurants and food options! As Amsterdam Photographer I always recommend this place to clients at then end of my Amsterdam Photoshoot + Tour!

Name: Laura T.
Review: Super cute brunch spot, service was awesome, and food was bomb. The menu options and flavors were different from what I could get in the US. Must try when in Amsterdam!

Name: Craig G.
Review: For the last meal of my trip, I had to satisfy my craving for Indonesian. Sampurna is a sleek, cozy spot not far from the flower market in the city center. Reservations are recommend, as this place will fill up pretty quick, though I got there early enough to snag a table without a wait. As soon as you're seated, you're greeted with a bowl of rice crackers and three sambals (sauces, not unlike an Indian chutney). The menu features a number of satay skewers, a selection of rice dishes, and a few rijstafel (rice table: small portions of several dishes for a table to share). Dining solo, a rijstafel was out of the question, but the ayam penggang seten caught my eye.I'm pretty sure the literal translation of the dish is "fried chicken in Satan sauce", which seemed apt: this was one of the most brutally spicy dishes I've ever eaten. Aside from the intense heat, the dish was actually very flavourful, with garlic, lemongrass, galangal, and other spices shining through. Every entree here comes with a number of small side dishes: white rice, pickled veggies, veggies in a coconut curry sauce, and fried tempeh. Everything was delicious, all the better when washed down with a glass of Bintang (an Indonesian beer).The staff was friendly, but harried.

Name: Vy T.
Review: First off, the staff is witty and sarcastic, so if you cannot handle that, do not eat here. Period. Don't force yourself to like it otherwise you don't enjoy the food and be upset over the way they talk. Second, you need cash, otherwise it's a 15% service charge if you use plastic. There's an ATM across the street. Third, the portions are huge! So be prepared to togo or better yet, share with a friend while it's pipping hot and delicious. A sharing plate is an extra 7 euros FYI. Fourth, this is great BBQ but not worth more than a 30min wait imo. I heard wait times can be 2hrs+. Coming from the States, we have great BBQ also, so I'm likely slightly biased in this sense. Anyhow, so fortunately, we were able to be seated right away outside. We ordered the smoked ribs, a 24oz filet, and a baked potato. The food also comes with cole slaw and bread. As mentioned, the portions were huge! We wished we took this into account before ordering as we had a lot of leftover, our starving selves could not finish it all. Smoked ribs - amazing. The meat fell right off the bone and it wasn't too smoky at all. I got about 20 large bones, delicious. I was thankful for the bread to eat with it as it was a lot of meat. 24oz Filet - cooked to a perfect medium rare and also delicious. Cole slaw was good and helped cut the meat down as well. Overall good but again, I don't think it's worth waiting more than 30mins and please don't eat here if you are expecting that "American service". It doesn't exist here. They are witty and sarcastic.

Name: Anna I.
Review: Foodhallen should be considered a tourist attraction in Amsterdam because it's literally amazing. It's basically a hall which different food vendors similar to a market. The food options are absolutely amazing. The hall, itself, is beautiful and the bathrooms are very clean. They have a lot of tables but it does get crowded. You'd be surprised how packed it could get. My partner and I shared a chicken pita wrap and ordered a burger from the Butcher. The burger was literally life changing. It was one of the most delicious, perfectly cooked, perfectly seasoned and freshest burgers I've ever had. My grammar is all over the place, but I think you get the point. The Butcher is definitely worth the long line and wait. I think anyone can find a good place at this Food Hall. If you're a vegan, vegetarian, pescatarian or a meat eater.

Name: Andrea W.
Review: Cool space, but it gets crowded with so many people. There was also a live band which made it difficult to chat. There are many choices of different international cuisines, but food is really pricey for small portions. I tried Viet View's spring rolls, Txosta's pintxos, and Lima's tacos, which were all just average. It's a good place to walk around to take a look, but I would recommend eating elsewhere.

Name: Dee K.
Review: I had tried repeatedly to make reservations from the states prior to our arrival with no such luck. Walked in around 6:30 on a Friday night and scored the last empty table. Line formed immediately after us. Service was amazing- friendly and attentive. Loved the ode to mothers everywhere adorning their walls. We each got the rice dish (sampler) for two which included a sampling of all the traditional offerings. It was delicious!!

Name: Nicole M.
Review: It is SO hot in here! Super stuffy - they need some fans or some air circulation going through this place.That aside though, it's a pretty cool spot. Lots of different eateries to choose from so there's something for everyone. First time trying bitterballen and that was fun with all the different flavors. The pizza from Renatos was delicious with lots of prosciutto in it. The hummus plate from Maza was pretty good but the tacos from Taqueria Lima were only okay.  And then there were places that, coming from SF, I'd never get something from - €5 for 3 pieces of dim sum from Dim Sum Thing is outrageous. But then again if I hadn't had dim sum in a while, who knows what money I'd pay for a fix.We came on a Friday night so it was understandably crowded, and it took over half an hour to finally get a full table for our party of 7. Good spot though for people to kick back with friends after work.

Name: Rowena P.
Review: Really cool vibe and yummy food in a back alley of the streets of Amsterdam. Definitely recommend for anyone who wants to be right in the scene for a good break before a night out.

Name: Michael S.
Review: Service, meal prep and presentation was excellent.  We had the fillet and the halibut, both were delightful.  We were able to get a nice table without a reservation, the historic building is warm and welcoming.  Overall a great experience.

Name: Van B.
Review: [VARIETY] now it is nearly a year ago when we ate at the foodhallen BUT I remember all & we are about to be there again soonish so I will update if necessary!You can order from a big variety of different places offering different dishes. Most of them are "small" portions. As we wanted to share & try as much as possible the portions are great. My partner mostly ordered something vegan|vegetarian for me and something meaty for him.Everything tasted really fresh & special. Quality 100%

Name: Enkrypt L.
Review: Best ribs my wife and I have ever had. Ever. I don't even like ribs that much, she loves them, but we were both just blown away. The lady's portion or whatever they call it is a real thing, don't be afraid to opt for it if you aren't feeling ravenous. Sides are absolutely unnecessary. Our bartender was also awesome and hilarious, and he had great recommendations for what else to do in the city, including a neighboring coffeeshop for the necessary supplies if you need to work up an appetite to finish your leftovers. Oh and almost the best part, if there's a wait, you just cross the street to the pub that has the same owner and drink a beer or two before your seats are ready. And unlike Café De Klos, the bar actually has a great beer selection too.

Name: Parker M.
Review: We came here for dinner while in Amsterdam. Be warned: they don't take reservations, and wait times can be lengthy (we waited nearly an hour). That said, this place without a doubt has the best (dry) ribs I've ever had (and I personally prefer dry rubs). Not to be outdone, the garlic butter is also the best butter (of any sort) I've ever come across.On top of that, this place might have the best service I've ever encountered--quick, attentive, and honest. When I mentioned my interest in getting a dessert, I was told without hesitation that the desserts would pale in comparison to the entree and that I'd be better off going round the corner to a pastry shop.

Name: Shelby W.
Review: My boyfriend and I wanted to try some Dutch food and get a real feel for Amsterdam. We took the Metro to have dinner here and it was packed both inside and on the patio! The wait time for 2 people would have been an hour. No worries.. We'll try again tomorrow night and now we know to make a reservation.We went back the next night and got the spinach potatoes with sausage and bacon. It came with a delicious and large salad as well as a dessert for 15 euros. The food was amazing! The plates of food may not look that large, but those potatoes sure do full you up! We weren't able to finish all of ours.The service was friendly, great prices, and good beer on tap. Definitely recommend! Best dinner I ate during my 5 days in Amsterdam! ****Don't forget to make your reservation!!!!!*****

Name: Charlotte S.
Review: First time traditional Dutch cuisine I was impressed with combination of flavors. Well balanced portions from Starters to Dessert. Nice atmosphere can see why it had so many 5 star reviews.

Name: Bob B.
Review: Went here for Dutch experience and was not disappointed. The waitress Jaime Joy was fantastic very attentive to our needs!  The halibut and seafood risotto did not disappoint. The Van Speyk salad was exceptional. Highly recommend this restaurant

Name: Joshua B.
Review: The pantryI came here with my husband to try out some Dutch food. We ordered the special #1 and #2. Menu 1:Pea soup - good, but not spectacular or special in any way. 3 mounds - they had certain flavors such as sauerkraut, kale, and one other one. They were decent. Vlaflip - my husband described it as dannon yogurt. And he's kinda right. :/ there was nothing really special about it Menu 2:Goat cheese croquettes - these were actually good, and I don't like goat cheese. Guess that's what happens when you deep fry anything though Ground beef, cauliflower, and mashed potatoes - just like shepherds pie. It was actually kinda bland, but it felt healthy due to the cauliflower. Really filling. Poffertjes aka mini pancakes - was the highlight of our mealOverall I would say that 1) the decor is cool 2) it's a very touristy restaurant 3) the food overall wasn't that good / maybe I'm just not super into Dutch food. 4) service was quite slow5) maybe was a bit overpriced for what it was I would not actually recommend this place. Also the fact that cigarette smoke from the outside kept coming in was very bothersome

Name: Maria E.
Review: *They close pretty early (4pm), FYI.Busy spot! We tried to get a table but the wait was over an hour. We put our name on the list and went to the Van Gogh museum. They called us while we were at the museum. We made it over there a little later but luckily they were still able to find us a table. This was on a Sunday by the way so it likely calms down during the week. Cute place with charming decor. Great menu options. I had the smoked salmon stack and it was really tasty. Friendly service. One complaint: the tables were a bit close together. I had someone directly behind me elbowing me.

Name: Emily W.
Review: Busy and bustling cafe but we got right in! It's a little noisy as all tables were filled but very nice energy. We started with a delicious matcha latte and orange juice. I enjoyed the Vege Brekkie - a flavorful sampling of veggies, eggs, halloumi cheese and toast. I would buy the chili jam by the bottle if I could! He enjoyed the Eggs Benny - perfectly cooked poached eggs atop bacon and toast topped with hollandaise. Everything was delicious and we left very full and satisfied. They are up front that the prices are not cheap but fair, quality ingredients are worth the price.

Name: Melissa N.
Review: What a cool vibe in Amsterdam.We were sat near the doors at a 2 top table and it was a pretty loud bar/night scene even on a random weekday.We got the ribs, bitter ballen, corn, and jerk chicken and somehow finished everything. I was surprised at myself for being able to put away the entire rack, the bitterballen and a piece of corn - I really should stop eating so much...lolWe got there around midnight and it was great that they were still serving food until like 2AM because many places stopped serving food much earlier.We had a really cool waitress as well. The staff was chill and we were able to take our time and still get a nice meal.I'd come back!

Name: Michael P.
Review: This was the first meal my girlfriend and I ate when we arrived in Amsterdam. Absolutely delicious! This is actual BBQ (surprising I know!) We both had the mixed ribs (smoked spare ribs & spare ribs), both were great but the regular spare ribs were fall off the bone juicy! The meals came with bread and a traditional Dutch salad. These are closer to being American sized portions rather than European. We sat and shot the shit and talked about music and traveling with the bartenders/servers for over two hours. They had the normal beers (Amstel, Heineken, etc) but you have to try De Blonde Barbier and De Manke Monnik (ones a blonde and ones a tripel, but both delicious). Definitely make this a stop if your in Amsterdam

Name: Fay T.
Review: Nice and easy cafe next Heineken experience hall. Good for 1-2 for a brunch and cup of coffee.

Name: Earl H.
Review: Amsterdam isn't exactly a culinary wonderland but it has some local flavors you shouldn't miss. The Pantry serves up typical Dutch cuisine with some of the friendliest service you'll find in Amsterdam.   I went for the zuurkoolstamppot which is Sauerkraut mixed into mashed potatoes with a sausage. Nothing exciting to look at but it was actually pretty delicious. If you're in Amsterdam I'd highly recommend making reservations and give the pantry a shot.

Name: Maria P.
Review: We wanted to try Indonesian cuisine while we were in Amsterdam since we've heard some pretty great things about it.  Sampurna was a convenient walk away from our hotel and they were open pretty late while everything seemed to be closed or was closing.  It's easy to find as they are located right next to the Bloemenmarkt (floating flower market).  We walked into the restaurant and were greeted & seated right away.  The restaurant was pretty empty and we had the section all to ourself, perfect!It was my first time trying Indonesian food and I was quite amused that a lot of the menu items were familiar terms used in Filipino languages.  Now, I told my husband that I wasn't that hungry, but somehow he managed to order the Rijtafel which is a whole spread of food that took up the entire table.  I definitely gave him "the look" but hey we were on our honeymoon and the food came out rather quickly.  Not to mention the prices were affordable for the amount of food that we got (A LOT), even in such a touristy area.  Everything was laid out so nicely and perfectly organized in several small, shared plates.  We had a sampling of a number of dishes and our meal came with little sauces/spices which I wanted to try out first. The first thing that I tried was out of this world spicy (It smelled similar to something used in Filipino cuisine & I am not a big fan of spicy food).  I wanted to cry, but my husband had a good laugh!  It's hilarious now that I can look back on it, but it wasn't at the time.  I learned after that to stick to the more milder flavored dishes which were oh so tasty.  Overall, good meal & I would recommend it if you're looking to try Indonesian cuisine and want to have the rice table experience (Rijtafel).  Just be prepared for the spiciness.  I was not, Lol.

Name: Veronika B.
Review: FoodHallen is an awesome food court with a ton of options. Whatever you eat, they have it! Came here on a Sunday at a very busy time and I was able to get a seat. It's super informal, everybody who helped me was super friendly. I ate the portobello burger from Padron, Dutch vegan cuisine, and it was definitely fantastic! If you need to charge your phone while you eat they have lockers for 1.5euro. Besides the food hall there are a bunch of unique shops and galleries inside and a free bike parking garage underground. Everything is priced reasonably, great atmosphere.

Name: Jennifer O.
Review: This place was awesome! There were so many food and drink options all under one roof. The worst part was trying to decide what to order. There were several areas to hang out within the food hall that were comfortable. Definitely a must try!

Name: Stella T.
Review: We walked in on a whim, no reservations. The place was jam packed! The friendly hostess was very accommodating in getting us seated fairly quickly. We ordered drinks which came out quick & really spot on perfectly made. The menu is in correlation with the namesake, lots of meat offerings. I ordered the classic burger & the bf ordered ribs. My burger was a tad salty but really good but his ribs! Oooooh man! Those were some serious finger licking ribs! We really enjoyed ourselves here & I highly recommend checking this place out. It's only fair that I pass on the baton since I found this gem through yelp.

Name: Meetu M.
Review: Very good food and introduction to Indonesian food.  Highly recommend this restaurant. Overall great dining experience!

Name: Mike C.
Review: All you folks looking for a dive bar with Amazing Food and Belgian Beers, the place IS IT!!!The decor is Dutch classic and they've easily had the best 80s/90s music playing since I walked in (Nirvana, The Cult, Michael Jackson...). Order the Ribs. The cook honestly carried the last rack to me with tongs from off THE PIT!

Name: Neluta G.
Review: Unfortunately this place did not impress. I was excited about it but it was disappointing. The dish I had "duck" not very good and they were kind enough to take it off the bill. I did explain that I do not care about that, I only care about the food experience but the guy that it is in charge of the menu insisted.The restaurant has these beautiful chandeliers, it brings you back to a Victorian era.Wine was OK, service was good. Lot's of restaurants in Amsterdam so...... there are many other choices.

Name: David B.
Review: Options for everybody. Great food. Cool place. I just can't seem to leave the taco place alone, though there are so many other options! I try to go with a large group of friends so we can do buffet style and try lots of different things.

Name: Tina Ø.
Review: Superb dinner and very good service - can highly be recommended. We will definitely be back

Name: Tyra L.
Review: I was very skeptical when this rib place was recommended to me. I'm from the US and of course we think we're the best at stuff, but I really did think bbq was our thing. However, I do think these were some of the best ribs I've ever had. ( I'm from the Midwest so take it for what it's worth.) The rub or whatever they pup on them is just perfect. I was traveling solo for the day, but there were many other loners sitting inside at the bar with me. Pretty sure the bar is the only spot they let you have if you're alone so beware. It is also not air conditioned inside so it was a little warm on an 80+ degree day (Fahrenheit... to be clear) If you pay with credit card they charge you an extra 5%.

Name: Jane C.
Review: Must visit when in Amsterdam! We made reservations in advance and happy we did. The restaurant was packed at 6 pm! Service is super quick and friendly. Food was amazing!

Name: Brenda E.
Review: I read about Van Speyk and reserved a table prior to our visit. No walk-in service is available and rightfully so. The food was carefully prepared and the presentation was beautiful. Each dish we had was delicious and the experience was amazing! Try the dark chocolate creme brulee!

Name: Gold C.
Review: Great ambiance both inside and outside. Service was fantastic and the food was equally impressive. Love the croquettes and the portobello mushroom! One block from Renaissance hotel and close to city center.

Name: Jenny P.
Review: Found this gem online. Wasn't sure what to expect but all the reviews recommended the ribs and the hodgepodge. Unfortunately the wife wasn't feeling to well so we were not able to eat at the restaurant so I went alone ordered a few items to go. The wife was a big fan of the stew which came as a recommendation from the staff and she could not have been happier. The spare ribs were also exceptional. Everyone there was very welcoming and the food was great too. Would recommend this place to anyone and everyone visiting Amsterdam!

Name: Rowena P.
Review: Really cool vibe and yummy food in a back alley of the streets of Amsterdam. Definitely recommend for anyone who wants to be right in the scene for a good break before a night out.

Name: Sylvia B.
Review: Love this place. Great for brunch! It gets busy but they will text you when your table is ready, which is really convenient. Highly recommend the navajo eggs, which come with perfectly poached eggs. They make a mean cortado as well!

Name: Pia M.
Review: 5 stars for Gin & Tonic bar.5 stars for the stand with the 5-cheese hot dog.5 stars for their great selection of beer.4 stars for the stand with the Jamon Iberico platters.There are lots of different vendors here like dim sum, sushi, seafood, burgers, tacos, tapas etc.  Although Yelp says they open until 1am, most stalls close between 10-11pm.  Also most of the stalls do not take cash, so make sure to bring a credit/debit card.Enjoy!!

Name: Brianne S.
Review: If you're in Amsterdam and love food this is definitely not a place to miss! Easy to reach by tram (just Google directions) this housed about 20 different food/drink vendors all under one roof. In a mood for Vietnamese? No problem. In a mood for Dim Sum? They got you! In a mood for a both and a side of tacos? This is your place! Seating here is definitely hard to come by but you'll find a spot or somewhere to stand and eat your food. You're going to keep on the move to get different things anyway. There is a great beer bar here with cans/bottles/drafts from all around the world, and an excellent gin & tonic bar across the way serving up real classy drinks to go along with anything you chose from the food hall. We were only in A'dam for a few days but I loved this place so much we came back twice to try even more! If ever we find ourselves back in town, this will most definitely be on the list to visit again!

Name: Rhonda W.
Review: we ate here the night we arrived and it was a lovely start to our trip. The concierge at our hotel   (the Renaissance  which a Marriott hotel)  recommended Van Speyk  .. showed us a menu and called to get us a reservation. We walked right over and were seated immediately which was very impressive on a  Friday night. Our server said it was fortunate that the concierge had called for us. This was my first experience with white asparagus and I LOVED it.          We started with escargot ... and bread.  I had the salmon with white asparagus , mash potatoes. My husband has a lamp chop with veggies .. a potato casserole and something that was like a spicy polenta ... but not sure what it was.  We both had a couple beers and enjoyed our meal. The service was fast and friendly until it came to getting the check and paying.  We found a good deal of the restaurants in Amsterdam  to be VERY slow to give you a check ..  we suspect that since tips aren't as common they aren't in any hurry to get you out of there.            The decor was lovely but the seating was a bit tight .. nice meal ... would recommend.

Name: TS R.
Review: Ok. If you want the authentic Dutch experience you can't get any better. Can't wait to return in May 2023.

Name: Lei G.
Review: Thoroughly enjoyed my lunch at Sampurna! It's located near the floating flower market but doesn't come across as stop for tourists. I'd been trying to get in more Indonesian meals while in Amsterdam. I do not know the names of any of my dishes, other than my ginger honey tea. The taste of the food was even better than the photos. The starter was tasty & delicate. The entree had two different types of veggies and the chicken was full of spices and the rice was done perfectly. The dessert was the cherry on top - it was coconut milk, green tapioca, much softer than typical tapioca with fresh sliced jackfruit. It'll be a dessert I'll be on the lookout for in the future!

Name: Bobby S.
Review: Food was good and would definitely recommend it. We were disappointed with the service. Long wait times and at the end, the server forced us to tip. I did bring to notice the average service and he came up with some excuse to justify it.

Name: David K.
Review: Customer service was excellent!!! My friend is a vegetarian and they made sure to cater a traditional Hutspot Dutch meal to her. The food was delicious. For the rest of us meat eaters, we ordered the Hutspot combination and bitterballen. Traditional Dutch food at its finest!!

Name: alvir n.
Review: Dead babies + top 50 hip hop. Classy.Vegan burger was delicious. Nachos were delicious. Aesthetics are on point.

Name: neil m.
Review: Pro: Very good cocktails, great atmosphere, reasonable price. Con: the menu is a hard piece of plastic that is cumbersome to use/open, our first server was a space cadet (didn't know drinks, ingredients, etc) but second person was amazing.

Name: Kelvin C.
Review: I think I came in here expecting something else, which was good ole fashioned-smoked american ribs slathered in tangy BBQ sauce.  Well, this wasn't it.  It's actually everything I stated above sans the BBQ sauce.  Instead they serve it with Hollandaise sauce as well as a side of Hollandaise "bbq" sauce...which is basically Hollandiase with a little bit of ketchup (I think).  The ribs were definitely smoked well and the meat was a bit leaner than what I'm used to so they don't fall of the bone.  Also, they provide you a MASSIVE amount of food for the price so if you order the mixed ribs plate, it is more than enough for two.  We also tried the french onion soup, which turned out to be better than what we had in france, and the tomato bisque soup, which was decent.  TIP: For a party of 2, don't be put off if the host tells you there is a two hour wait.  He's completely overestimating in order to weed out the curious people walking in that don't want to commit.  Simply head over to their bar right across the street and he'll come grab you in 45 minutes tops.4 stars.

Name: Gurpreet L.
Review: While Yelping places to grab a late dinner, we stumbled across Sampurna which was perfect for us because we had wanted to try Indonesian food in Amsterdam. We got here around 9:50 PM on a Thursday night and were told that kitchen was about to close (the restaurant closes at 11 PM but we learned that the kitchen closes at 10). We were quickly seated and scanned our options as quickly as possible so that we could get our order in. There were multiple vegetarian options for me to choose from which was a delightful surprise.I ended up picking the Tahu Bumbu Bali, a tofu dish, while my friend with what looked like a kebab plate. Our food was scrumptious! The tofu was perfectly crispy on the outside and it was smothered in this spicy sauce that had a perfect amount of kick. Although I was unable to try my friend's dish, from the way they were scarfing it down, I think they enjoyed their food. In a town with tons of Indonesian options, I highly recommend this place!

Name: Enkrypt L.
Review: Best ribs my wife and I have ever had. Ever. I don't even like ribs that much, she loves them, but we were both just blown away. The lady's portion or whatever they call it is a real thing, don't be afraid to opt for it if you aren't feeling ravenous. Sides are absolutely unnecessary. Our bartender was also awesome and hilarious, and he had great recommendations for what else to do in the city, including a neighboring coffeeshop for the necessary supplies if you need to work up an appetite to finish your leftovers. Oh and almost the best part, if there's a wait, you just cross the street to the pub that has the same owner and drink a beer or two before your seats are ready. And unlike Café De Klos, the bar actually has a great beer selection too.

Name: Marin J.
Review: Super cool spot with good variety! Bulls and dogs was decent but not as amazing as I'd hoped. The meatball was good but overpriced. Wings were ok. Too much to try, we need to go back!

Name: Jennifer O.
Review: This place was awesome! There were so many food and drink options all under one roof. The worst part was trying to decide what to order. There were several areas to hang out within the food hall that were comfortable. Definitely a must try!

Name: Cathy Z.
Review: Neat concept in Amsterdam a bit off the tourist block. This place seemed to have something for everyone! We shared a burrata board and some tacos. The tacos were honestly incredible. They were pulled chicken and had pickled onion on them. So good I should have ordered a platter! The burrata was nice too. They top it with some truffle oil. Not the best burrata I have but a tasty snack during the day.

Name: Ryan A.
Review: If you know me by now, I tend to make frequent stops at food halls, or indoor/outdoor markets as I find them to less touristy and more geared to locals (In most cases).De Foodhallen flirted with a tourist trap, but ultimately brought a locals vibe more than anything. It is the perfect place if going out with a bunch of friends who are very picky in terms of what they prefer to eat. It is littered with food stalls serving tasty meals from around the globe. Want ramen...they got it, want tacos...they got it, want hamburgers...they got it, want local bitterballens...I think you get the idea. Being a foodie, I was in heaven, I must of done four to five rounds before deciding on what I wanted. Being day six in the Netherlands and not having much local food, specifically the fried balls of goodness otherwise known as Bitterballen, I had to cave! They offer a platter with all different flavors at one of the stalls for a great price point. My travel partner decided she wanted a burger, a blue cheese to be specific. Both meals were phenomal, might I say one of the better while staying in Amsterdam. I will forewarn you, this place is popular, so much that seating can be a pain in the arse. If you have a friend(s) with you, it may be wise to split up with some finding seating depending how busy it is. Either way, make sure to bookmark this wonderful food hall, not only for their scrumptious food, but also their beer stalls and awesome lounge areas!

Name: Brittany S.
Review: Wine selection and food was outstanding. Fabulous steak! Cooked and seasoned to perfection.

Name: Shay H.
Review: Loved this restaurant! It's a real gem in Amsterdam. The decor indoors was very sweet and unique- filled with pictures of mothers. Food was delicious as well, and the portions were very generous. It reminded me a lot of home, both in the atmosphere and the comfort food.

Name: Sabrina S.
Review: This was my first time having a full Indonesian meal and it did not disappoint.  I really liked the appetizers that were included.  Food was fresh, delicious, and boldly flavored.  We were able to get in without a reservation without any issue, which I appreciated considering how packed the place was when we arrived.  I cannot really think of anything I didn't like, so 5 stars it is!

Name: Daniel F.
Review: Pretty good burger and meat for Europe in an American style joint. The fries are good. Overall a solid experience. It wasn't the best but bang for buck it's pretty good.

Name: Rowena P.
Review: Really cool vibe and yummy food in a back alley of the streets of Amsterdam. Definitely recommend for anyone who wants to be right in the scene for a good break before a night out.

Name: Marin J.
Review: Super cool spot with good variety! Bulls and dogs was decent but not as amazing as I'd hoped. The meatball was good but overpriced. Wings were ok. Too much to try, we need to go back!

Name: Leena R.
Review: I am absolutely in love with this place. I was in Amsterdam for a short trip and looking for a place with a relaxed atmosphere and great drinks where I could get a delicious birthday meal at midnight. Not exactly an easy find as most kitchens in the area closed down at 10pm except for a select few burger/fries spots, but our hotel concierge recommended Cannibale Royale. The ambiance is a nice mix between a restaurant and bar, with trendy decor and super friendly staff. The food is mouth-watering good, which is not an easy thing to find at midnight! I was able to get a huge ribeye steak and a side of some of the best Mac and cheese I've ever had. The beer selection is also pretty great. But the cherry on top of a great meal/drinks/service was when my boyfriend mentioned it was my birthday and our waiter brought out complimentary shots to take with us. We left in such good spirits that we came back the very next day with friends, who also loved it as much as we did. This was the perfect place to spend my birthday and I'll be back the next time I'm in Amsterdam!

Name: Craig G.
Review: For the last meal of my trip, I had to satisfy my craving for Indonesian. Sampurna is a sleek, cozy spot not far from the flower market in the city center. Reservations are recommend, as this place will fill up pretty quick, though I got there early enough to snag a table without a wait. As soon as you're seated, you're greeted with a bowl of rice crackers and three sambals (sauces, not unlike an Indian chutney). The menu features a number of satay skewers, a selection of rice dishes, and a few rijstafel (rice table: small portions of several dishes for a table to share). Dining solo, a rijstafel was out of the question, but the ayam penggang seten caught my eye.I'm pretty sure the literal translation of the dish is "fried chicken in Satan sauce", which seemed apt: this was one of the most brutally spicy dishes I've ever eaten. Aside from the intense heat, the dish was actually very flavourful, with garlic, lemongrass, galangal, and other spices shining through. Every entree here comes with a number of small side dishes: white rice, pickled veggies, veggies in a coconut curry sauce, and fried tempeh. Everything was delicious, all the better when washed down with a glass of Bintang (an Indonesian beer).The staff was friendly, but harried.

Name: Christine W.
Review: If you're a tourist in Amsterdam you might be thinking that you should try more typical Amsterdam foods BUT here's why you need to try out sampurna+++it's authentic - at least according to the bf who is from indonesia. We got the batara menu which like most of the other menus allowed a large variety of food sampling. If you aren't sure what to get, that's a greAt menu- faves were the chicken soup/fried dumplings/salad with light vinegrette +++the flavors were such an adventure- each dish was a delightful combo of a lot of tastes, spicy/fragrant/savory/even a hint of sweetness +++dessert was delicious - we got the es pisang goreng which is a fried plantain with delicious vanilla ice cream and whipped cream

Name: Brenda E.
Review: I read about Van Speyk and reserved a table prior to our visit. No walk-in service is available and rightfully so. The food was carefully prepared and the presentation was beautiful. Each dish we had was delicious and the experience was amazing! Try the dark chocolate creme brulee!

Name: Tim V.
Review: I was very skeptical about BBQ in Amsterdam; however, I have faith in my people...The spare ribs were the equivalent to nearly two racks of ribs in the states and rivaled almost any ribs I have ever had - almost. An amazing dry rub unlike any flavor I've had before. The staff was amazing, witty and obviously possessed Dutch sarcasm.

Name: alvir n.
Review: Dead babies + top 50 hip hop. Classy.Vegan burger was delicious. Nachos were delicious. Aesthetics are on point.

Name: Jacques I.
Review: What may be the best BBQ in Amsterdam! We came here based off its awesome Yelp reviews and the first time we visited the place was packed.  The wait was an hour or so, so we decided to come back on a different day, closer to when they open.  So glad we did, too, because it would've been sad to have missed these spare ribs during our visit to Amsterdam! Specifically, Cafe De Klos is known for its BBQ ribs.  After speaking with our server about the difference between the spare ribs and the smoked spare ribs, he mentioned that the spare ribs have a dry rub versus a hickory, smoky sauce on the smoked ones.  Personally, I'm a dry-rub fan and don't like my ribs sauced up, so stuck with the spare ribs, which I loved.  The spare ribs plate came with a side salad, which was a coleslaw, with two different kind of aioli sauces that you can use for your ribs.  Of the two sauces I preferred the white one, for its garlic flavor versus the tomato-based aioli.  Coleslaw was a good accompaniment for the ribs, adding a nice acidity with its pickled flavor.  And most importantly, the spare ribs were fall-off-the-bone, just how I like 'em!  The ribs were juicy, moist and had an awesome spiced rub on the skin.  The portion was large, but I happily ate all three racks of ribs.  There is a smaller portion option with two racks of ribs for you, amateurs. Cafe De Klos is definitely worth visiting in Amsterdam.  Expect a wait; BUT, its sister bar, Café t Genootschap der Geneugten is across the street, where you can grab drinks 'til an employee from Cafe De Klos will come get you once a table is available.  It's worth the wait.  Space is small inside, which is also why it takes a bit to get a table.  Most of the seating is around the bar.  If you do use your credit card there is a 5% additional charge; bring euros.  Spare ribs for the win here!

Name: M Y.
Review: Stopped by late in the evening. We were able to easily get a table for two. The interior is cozy and inviting. We ordered a few dishes including Mamma's happas, the Fisher's wife salad, and the pea soup. They were all delicious. I also really like the dishes they served the food in. Overall we had a great dining experience here. I'd definitely recommend having a meal at Moeders.

Name: Teryl R.
Review: Ran into this spot because the original spot was closed. First I would like to say that I appreciate the waitress for seating us without reservations (didn't know we needed because of last minute changes). We were seated quickly, and spaced out from other guests. I love how multiple people check with us to see if we needed anything at our table, great customer service. The food was just what we needed and the prices were reasonable. If I ever come back to Amsterdam I will make sure to stop by again.

Name: Karen S.
Review: Wow. I rarely go 5 stars, but this place is that good. The service was great. Super friendly and they all seem to enjoy being there. The food. I am probably in the minority for ordering the chicken, but it was delicious. Moist and flavorful - perfect! I really enjoyed the cole slaw/salad. A little tangy with kind of Italian dressing. Nice fresh crunchy side with all the decadent meat. The ribs were spot on. Husband liked both but the smoked had amazing flavor and char. Yum! We will definitely be back!

Name: Jackson S.
Review: There are a lot of choices to eat around here. Across the street is Italian that boasts "it's simply the best" and the place outside with a rowdy table has Dutch mussels and fries for 10 euros. So, why come here? Well, Yelp says it's good Dutch traditional food. It looks cute inside, may be 1930s style with porcelain plates and tassled fake candelabras on the wall, despite it only being open since 2000.As with all traditional restaurants, The Pantry does a bustling tourist trade. Is that good or bad? Neither. Everyone's having fun, and they welcome lone diners like me. In fact I even lucked out and got a window table on a pleasant late summer night ( no rain, 60F). If you don't might the occasional waft of cigarettes coming into your meal it's a nice spot.I ordered combo of hutspot (mashed potato with beef and veg) boerenkoolstamppot (mashed potato, kale and bacon) and zuurkoolstamppot (mashed potato with sauerkraut). It was tasty, although a bit salty, esp the bacon dish. I got the yogurt and custard dessert which was as it sounded. An odd combo, but tasty. You're supposed to mix it together, but I ate it separately.All, in all a nicer dining experience than the other places in this area. The host / server was really friendly and humorous. The place as packed. I tried another Dutch restaurant in another part of town and it was better, but more expensive.
